newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks rebound at close, seen wary.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks rebound at close, seen wary.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed moderately higher Friday, erasing early losses, but the outlook for next week remained conditioned by the erratic swings on Wall Street, dealers said.

"Today we were glued to Wall Street every step of the way -- our late recovery followed the Dow's bounceback with no other good explanation," one trader said, reflecting the prevailing sense of frustration after mixed reactions in New York to the key March jobs report.
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 0.6 percent to 722.42, paring losses in the week to 2.3 percent.

"The bolsa will remain cautious and conditioned by developments abroad which dictate ADR movements, but it may have found some technical support at 720," said analyst Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
He said if cash flows picked up and Wall Street steadied, the MerVal could aim for 740 in the near term.
"We also have to keep an eye on Brazil, which fared very well today and could encourage local players not to reduce their exposure any further," said Bonanno.
Brazilian stocks surged Friday on the back of a telephone rate hike which sent bellwether Telebras soaring.
Local floor volume picked up to 18.9 million pesos from 13.8 million Thursday, while over-the-counter turnover swelled to 138.2 million pesos from 72 million Thursday.
The broad market edged up 0.2 percent, with winners outpacing losers 32 to 20 and 17 issues closing flat.

Top main-tier performers were steelmaker Acindar and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, up 2.6 percent and 2.2 percent, respectively. Losers were led by Banco de Galicia, real estate developer Irsa and holding company Perez Companc, off 1.5 percent, 1.3 percent and 0.9 percent respectively.
